answer: Count the replication cost first, then the reward. Each identity funds its own overhead, and that overhead vests in a slow stream released over months. Auditors rotate out of a shared pool, so no reviewer sees the same submitter twice in a cycle. A farm of a thousand clones pays a thousand overheads up front, holds them through every dawn of the vesting curve, and still meets a fresh pool at each check. Cargo only leaves the wharf after the last review clears, so the plume of payouts arrives long after the clones have burned their budget.
